title: Look up a name
starter:
let rec lookup name items =
  None
hints: Match on `items`. An empty list holds no names at all, so that case is `None`.
The other case is `(n, p) :: rest`: the first pair, taken apart, in front of the rest. Compare `n` with `name`.
`| (n, p) :: rest -> if n = name then Some p else lookup name rest`
explain: An empty list has no answer, so it gives `None`. Otherwise the first pair is `(n, p)`. When `n` equals `name` the answer is `Some p`. When it does not, the answer is whatever the lookup finds in `rest`, which may be `None` in the end.
